title.narrative: Diakonia: Supporting People for a Dignified Life 2020-2024
Diakonia: Supporting People for a Dignified Life 2020-2024

description.narrative: Programmet inriktar sig på att bidra till ett rättvist, jämlikt och hållbart Kambodja fritt från fattigdom, förtryck, ojämlikhet och våld. Det övergripande målet för programmet är: Ett stärkt civilsamhälle med kapacitet att utvidga det demokratiska utrymmet och främja mänskliga rättigheter och jämställdhet så att människor i Kambodja kan leva ett fredligt och värdigt liv med tillgång till grundläggande rättigheter och friheter. Det övergripande målet har fyra underliggande mål; 1) Mål för mänskliga rättigheter: Rättighetsinnehavares, gräsrotssamhällens och civilsamhällesorganisationers kapacitet stärks så att de kan förespråka en fungerande rättsstat samt respekt för och främjande av mänskliga rättigheter, vilket gynnar alla. 2) Mål för demokrati: Stöd till rättighetsinnehavare, gräsrotssamhällen och civilsamhällesorganisationer för att stärka deras förmåga att utvidga det demokratiska utrymmet i Kambodja, vilket gynnar alla. 3) Jämställdhetsmål: Kvinnor, män, pojkar och flickor ska ges inflytande och stärkas så att de kan utöva sina rättigheter för jämställdhet, hålla regeringen ansvarig för sina åtaganden och bidra till att minska det könsrelaterade våldet i samhället. 4) Mål för att stärka partnerna: Partnerna ges möjlighet och stärks för att uppnå organisatorisk och programmässig hållbarhet. Under 2023 omfattade programmet 17 implementerande kambodjanska civilsamhälles organisationer.

The program aims to contribute to a just, equal and sustainable Cambodia free from poverty, oppression, inequality and violence. The overall objective for the program is; A strengthened civil society with the capacity to widen democratic space and promote human rights and gender equality so Cambodian people can lead peaceful, dignified lives with access to fundamental rights and freedoms. The four underlying objectives are; 1) Human Rights Objective: Rights holders', grassroots communities', and CSO's capacity strengthened to advocate for a functioning rule of law as well as respect and promotion of Human Rights, which benefits all. 2) Democracy Objective: Rights holders, grassroots communities and CSOs supported to strengthen their capability for widening democratic space in Cambodia, which benefits all. 3) Gender Equality Objective: Women, men and boys and girls empowered and strengthened to exercise their rights for gender equality, hold government accountable to their commitments and contribute to reducing gender-based violence in community and society. 4) Objectives for strengthening partners: Partners are empowered and strengthened to achieve organizational and programmatic sustainability. In 2023 the program included 17 implementing Cambodian civil society organisations.

The overall objective for the program is; A strengthened civil society with the capacity to widen democratic space and promote human rights and gender equality so Cambodian people can lead peaceful, dignified lives with access to fundamental rights and freedoms. The overall objective has four underlying objectives that will all contribute to a strengthened civil society. The objectives are; 1) Human Rights Objective: Rights holders', grassroots communities', and CSO's capacity strengthened to advocate for a functioning rule of law as well as respect and promotion of Human Rights, which benefits all. 2) Democracy Objective: Rights holders, grassroots communities and CSOs supported to strengthen their capability for widening democratic space in Cambodia, which benefits all. 3) Gender Equality Objective: Women, men and boys and girls empowered and strengthened to exercise their rights for gender equality, hold government accountable to their commitments and contribute to reducing gender-based violence in community and society. 4) Objectives for strengthening partners: Partners are empowered and strengthened to achieve organizational and programmatic sustainability.

In 2024 the program has provided core support to 16 key human rights organisations in Cambodia in accordance with the program document and the agreement, including approved updated workplan and budget. The programme has achieved significant results and is in progress to achieive it's objectives. However, there has also been challenges, many in relation to the context of the closing space for civil society. Overall, the programme's focus on human rights and opportunities for core support to civil society is assessed to have played a significant role in the context and contributes to creating some room for positive forces to work for changes in the long term. One example of results achieved by implementing partners is the work of the women's rights organization Banteay Srey (BS). BS has, with the help of core support through Diakonia, succesfully worked to strengthen Cambodian women's rights at the local level where they, among other things, train local contact persons (community facilitators) who work in close collaboration with female municipal officials responsible for issues relating to women and children. An example of activities carried out is workshops with crosssectoral working groups on genderbased violence with relevant actors at village, municipal, district and provincial level, where one of the topics is the distribution of budget to survivors of genderbased violence. BS report that their longterm work with capacity building of local authorities on gender equality has led to 22 of the 44 municipalities in the provinces of Siem Reap and Battambang (targeted by their activities) increasing their gender responsive budgets. The increase from 2022 to 2023 was on average 38% for the municipalities of Battambang and 21% for the municipalities of Siem Reap
